identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is a daily pre-shift inspection log for a Toyota forklift (model 8FGU25) at the Portland warehouse, tracking thirteen safety-critical systems under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). Each inspection marks components as passing (✓) or defective (X), with operators signing and noting any problems; this document is current through mid-September 2026 and shows one defect flagged on September 9.
scan.freshness_note: Log entries end on 2026-09-17, now 12 days old. Current daily entries should be produced to demonstrate ongoing compliance.

conditions.title: Daily pre-shift examination before equipment placed in service
conditions.evidence_expected: Completed inspection log with date, shift, operator name, all checklist items marked (✓ or X), hours, and sign-off; defects immediately reported and corrected before use.

conditions.title: Equipment not used if examination reveals a safety defect
conditions.evidence_expected: Notation in log (as shown Sep 9: 'Horn not working') and maintenance record confirming defect corrected before return to service.

conditions.title: Defects reported and corrected immediately
conditions.evidence_expected: Log entries noting defects, maintenance work order, and follow-up inspection confirming repair before equipment resumes operation.

expected_missing.title: Operator training and certification records
expected_missing.why: OSHA 1910.178(l) requires documented training and evaluation before anyone operates a truck, with re-evaluation at least every three years.
expected_missing.basis: Similar companies maintain separate operator certifications; the log names operators (M.C., J.R.) but does not show when they were trained or when re-evaluation is due.

expected_missing.title: Defect correction and follow-up inspection record
expected_missing.why: When a defect is found (such as 'Horn not working' on Sep 9), OSHA requires the truck be removed from service and corrected immediately; follow-up inspection showing the repair and return to service are not shown in this log.
expected_missing.basis: OSHA 1910.178(q)(7) requires defects be reported and corrected, with no return to service until safe. The Sep 9 entry notes 'Horn not working' but later entries do not show verification the horn was repaired and inspected before the truck was used again.

expected_missing.title: Equipment maintenance history and parts records
expected_missing.why: To demonstrate that defects are tracked and corrected, maintenance work orders and parts replacement records support the pre-shift log.
expected_missing.basis: Similar companies maintain maintenance files tied to inspection logs to prove defects have been addressed.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on what the document is, its format, and which defect was noted (Sep 9 horn failure). High confidence that this is a record, not a permit or policy, and that it is current through September 17. The OSHA standard 1910.178(q)(7) is well-established and the inspection checklist aligns with the cited regulation. Medium confidence on whether the Sep 9 defect was corrected before the truck was used again—the log itself does not show this. The operators named (M.C., J.R.) are initials only; full training and certification records are not in this document. The log is 12 days old as of the query date (2026-09-29), so current compliance would require ongoing daily entries not shown here.
